title: copilot tools / Generate and test agent code
content: ## Generate and test agent code **Get Agent Code Generation Best Practices** supplies instructions that complement the Microsoft Foundry skill. Use it to guide {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %}'s code changes for the scenario and model you tested. 1. In the project folder, ask {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} to create the agent. Replace `` with the deployment you selected: ```prompt Create a Python agent with Microsoft Agent Framework that summarizes support notes into three bullet points. Use my selected Foundry Toolkit project and its existing model deployment named . Use Foundry Toolkit agent development guidance. Include setup instructions and {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} configurations for local debugging with Agent Inspector. Do not provision new Azure resources or deploy the agent yet. ``` 2. Confirm the project and deployment when {% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} requests them. Review the proposed changes before accepting them. Check the instructions, dependencies, credential handling, entry point, and model deployment configuration. 3. Save the files you intend to keep. For the Python debugging path, check that `.vscode` configurations are at the workspace root so {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} can find them. 4. Follow the generated project's setup instructions, then [run and test the agent locally](/docs/intelligentapps/hosted-agents.md#run-and-test-locally). Use its generated debug configuration with `F5` when available. 5. In [Agent Inspector](/docs/intelligentapps/agent-inspector.md#use-the-inspector), send the same support note you tested in the Playground and review the response. Repeat after changing the instructions. Opening Inspector alone does not start the agent server. Generated code and debug configuration require review and execution; they are not proof that the agent works or is deployed. If you later add tools, test a request that requires a real tool result and inspect its inputs and output. A model-only answer or a mocked result does not verify the live integration. For shared connections and tool prerequisites, use [Tool Catalog](/docs/intelligentapps/tool-catalog.md).
